transcript.text: Bosch SMS25AW00G, came back to E:09 on the display and the dishes are washed but stone cold. Is this an expensive fix?

On your Bosch SMS25AW00G, E:09 indicates a flow-through heating element or heating circuit failure. This is typically not an expensive fix; it usually involves checking the heater assembly (often integrated with the circulation pump) or the temperature sensor, rather than the main control board. However, to be certain this isn't just a setting issue, I need to confirm if the machine is genuinely failing to heat water. Could you run an intensive or 65°C programme with a normal load and tell me if the dishes come out hot and steamy, or still cold?
Both the hot programme and eco come out cold. Last three runs it's been the same, and the water felt cold to the touch mid-cycle too. Does that point to the heater?

The fact that the water was genuinely cold mid-cycle suggests a genuine heating failure rather than just poor drying. On your Bosch model, E:09 specifically points to the flow-through heating element or its circuit. Because this machine uses a flow-through heater integrated into the circulation pump assembly (rather than a separate exposed element at the bottom), the most likely cause is that the heater unit itself has failed. This is typically not an expensive fix; it involves checking the pump/heater assembly or, less commonly, checking the temperature sensor or wiring loom. I would recommend calling an engineer to check the flow-through heater/pump assembly.

candidates: Heating element / flow-through heater assembly failure (high)
NTC temperature sensor or wiring fault (medium)
